quotes.citation: འདུལ་བའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — the same printer's verse at the end of Chökyi Gyaltsen's Vinaya general meaning, in this edition's closing matter
quotes.why: The one place in the archive where the verse is given an explicit heading of authorship: it is the printing-colophon prayer 'spoken by Gongsa Chok', the honorific for the Dalai Lama — not a verse of Chökyi Gyaltsen's.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — the verse's own prose colophon, immediately after it (p426 of this text)
quotes.why: The verse's author states its purpose and its scope in his own words: a dedication-prayer for the printing of any Buddhist scripture of any tenet system, composed by Ngawang Lobsang Tenzin Gyatso.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་བཞི་པའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — the chapter-closing (སྐབས་བསྡུ་བ) of the fourth-chapter volume of the same series
quotes.why: What the author's own close of a chapter looks like in this series — a formal སྐབས་བསྡུ་བ naming the work — which the first-chapter volume, as transcribed here, passes straight over into the printer's verse.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། — end of the first-chapter mtha' dpyod, just before the same printer's verse
quotes.why: The companion volume carries two layers of closing verse: one written for this tradition, praying that Chökyi Gyaltsen's system flourish, and then the generic printer's verse of p425 — which shows by contrast how little the latter is tied to this text.

quotes.citation: Maitreya, Abhisamayālaṃkāra (Tengyur, sher phyin ka, Toh. 3786) — the closing colophon
quotes.why: The canonical Ornament ends at its translators' colophon; the dedication verse that follows it in the modern printed Ornament in this archive is absent from the Tengyur text.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 7 (JA)/TD03793_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I 'GREL PA (Abhisamayālaṃkāra Nāma Prajñā Pāramita Upadeśa Śāstra Vṛtti)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Haribhadra, Abhisamayālaṃkāravṛtti (འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ།, Tengyur Toh. 3793) — the author's final verse
quotes.why: Haribhadra's own closing verse, the last words before his colophon in the canonical text; the canonical Vṛtti, like the canonical Ornament, carries no printer's dedication.

quotes.text: དཔེར་ན། རྒྱ་མཚོ་ཆེན་པོའི་ཕྱོགས་བཞི་ནས་སྐྱེས་བུ་བཞི་ཆུ་འཆུ་ན། དེ་ཐམས་ཅད་འདི་ལྟ་སྟེ ། ལན་ཚྭའི་རོར་རོ་གཅིག་པ་ཉིད་དུ་འཆུ་ཞིང་ལེན་ཏོ། །འཇམ་དཔལ། དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ངས་ཆོས་གང་ཅི་བསྟན་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ནི། འདི་ལྟ་སྟེ། སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པའི་རོ་དང། དངོས་པོ་མེད་པའི་རོ་དང། འདོད་ཆགས་དང་བྲལ་བའི་རོ་དང། རྣམ་པར་གྲོལ་བའི་རོ་དང། འགོག་པའི་རོར་རོ་གཅིག་གོ
quotes.citation: Saptaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā (Kangyur, sher phyin sna tshogs ka) — the ocean simile addressed to Mañjuśrī
quotes.why: A Prajñāpāramitā sūtra's own statement of the image the verse opens with: every teaching is 'of one taste' as the ocean is of one taste, and among the tastes named is the taste of liberation. Found by my own search; offered as the image's canonical background, not as a source the verse cites.

quotes.citation: Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Kangyur, mdo mang ja) — the rain-cloud and plants chapter, addressed to Kāśyapa
quotes.why: The second canonical locus of 'one taste — the taste of liberation', in the parable where one rain waters plants of every size: the verse's rivers of teaching that all run to one ocean belong to this family of images. Found by my own search.
